newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 19.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* Marriott agreed to buy Hong Kong-based Renaissance Hotel Group for $947 million, plus the assumption of $53.2 million in debt. The pact gives Renaissance shareholders $30 a share, more than 10 percent above what they would have gotten in Doubletree's proposal.

* Evergreen Media will buy Chancellor Broadcasting in a stock swap worth $567 million. The combined company will then buy 10 stations from Viacom for $1.08 billion, becoming the nation's No. 2 radio chain.
* H.F. Ahmanson's hostile bid to buy Great Western Financial for $6.59 billion could trigger a takeover battle between the nation's No. 1 and No. 2 thrifts.
* Natural-gas seller NGC agreed to buy electricity producer Destec for $21.67 a share and said it will sell Destec's international operations to AES Corp for $365 million.
* Hewlett-Packard reported its fiscal first quarter profits rose 15 percent, posting earnings of $0.87 per share. The gain was made mostly by cutting costs.
* Phillip Rooney, chief executive of troubled waste management company WMX, said he would resign, and the company's shares rose 5.3 percent.
* The Dow industrials rose 78.50 to 7,067.46. Bond prices fell and the dollar dropped.
* An Arizona real-estate group has acquired nearly 30 percent of the prime commercial property in downtown San Diego, including a $65 million landmark building.
* The Supreme Court ruled that workers who accuse employers of job discrimination are protected against retaliation under federal laws, even after they leave their companies.
* Charles Schwab is seeking to give its customers a way to hire private money managers.
* Cablevision said it is willing to buy ITT's 50 percent stake in Madison Square Garden for more than $500 million.
* Apple said Executive Vice President Marco Landi resigned, the latest in a series of high-level departures.
* Teledesic said it is exploring a design that would let its communications company start operating with only a third of its planned satellites in orbit.
* Heart on the Street and Credit Markets were not immediately available on the paper's electronic service.
